basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 25.' and it opens 'Vers. 25. Portantes stacten in Aegyptum. Stacte gutta myrrhae arboris, quamvis et ipsa'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 25. Portantes stacten in Aegyptum. Stacte gutta myrrhae arboris, quamvis et ipsa myrrha vocetur. Extractio Joseph de cisterna resurrectionem significat Christi.
